{
  "title": "Cruz and Phoenix and the Brick That Clicked",
  "subtitle": "The first adventure of Bricky the glowing brick",
  "chapters": [
    {
      "heading": "Chapter 1: The Carpenter in Billund",
      "text": "Cruz lay on his bedroom floor, way past bedtime, snapping LEGO pieces onto a big grey shark. Its fin kept popping off. Phoenix sat beside him, walking a little plastic dinosaur across the carpet, roaring very quietly so nobody upstairs would hear.

"Stupid fin," Cruz whispered, pressing it down again. **POP.** Off it came.

Then one plain little brick, all alone in the pile, started to glow. Soft and yellow, like a nightlight.

"Cruz," whispered Phoenix. "Brick is GLOWING."

The brick wiggled. Two tiny eyes blinked open, and it grew a wobbly little smile.

"Hello," said the brick. "I'm Bricky. Want to know a secret about why bricks click — and why yours doesn't, yet? Come on."

**WHOOOOSH!** The bedroom folded away like paper, and Cruz and Phoenix landed in a little green town with red rooftops.

"This is **Billund, Denmark**," said Bricky. "In **1932**, a carpenter named **Ole Kirk Christiansen** started making wooden toys right here, in a small workshop."

A kind man with sawdust on his apron was carving a little wooden duck on wheels. He pulled a string and the duck waddled along, its wheels going CLACKA-CLACKA-CLACK.

"Families didn't have much money back then," Ole Kirk said, wiping his hands. "Nobody could buy new tables or chairs. But everybody could use a smile. So I made toys instead."

Phoenix laughed so hard at the waddling duck that he fell right over onto the grass.",
      "shout_line": "CLACKA-CLACKA-CLACK!"
    },
    {
      "heading": "Chapter 2: Play Well",
      "text": "**BZZZT.** A little bell rang inside the workshop, and Ole Kirk gathered everyone close, even Cruz and Phoenix.

"My toys need a name," he said. "Any ideas?"

Cruz thought about his shark, and how much he loved playing with it even with its silly floppy fin. "What about... something about playing?" he said.

Ole Kirk's eyes went wide, like Cruz had handed him a present. In **1934**, he mashed together two Danish words, **leg godt**, which mean **"play well."** Squash them together and you get **LEGO**.

"LEGO," said Phoenix, trying it out. "LEEEE-go."

Ole Kirk carved a wooden sign for the workshop wall. It said **"Only the best is good enough."**

"That's my promise," he told them. "Every toy, I make it the best I can."

"Even the duck?" asked Phoenix.

"Especially the duck," said Ole Kirk, and the duck went CLACKA-CLACKA-CLACK across the floor one more time, just to prove it.",
      "shout_line": "PLAY WELL!"
    },
    {
      "heading": "Chapter 3: The Workshop That Burned",
      "text": "One night, Bricky's glow flickered orange instead of yellow. "This part is a little sad," Bricky said gently, "but it turns out okay. I promise."

The sky over the workshop had turned red. **WHOOSH** — fire! In **1942**, the whole workshop burned down.

Cruz grabbed Phoenix's hand. "Is everyone safe?"

"Yes," said Bricky quickly. "Nobody was hurt. Not one single person. Just the building."

Ole Kirk stood in the ashes the next morning, looking at nothing where his workshop used to be. Then he rolled up his sleeves.

"Well," he said. "I suppose we build it bigger this time."

And he did. Board by board, the new workshop rose up even taller than before.

Phoenix patted a wooden beam like it was a good dinosaur. "You're okay now," he told it.

Cruz grinned. Sometimes the best thing to build again is exactly what you already had — just stronger.",
      "shout_line": null
    },
    {
      "heading": "Chapter 4: The Bricks That Wouldn't Stick",
      "text": "**Ding!** Years rolled by like a fast-forward button, and Bricky landed them in a workshop full of strange new toys made of shiny plastic.

"These are called **Automatic Binding Bricks**," said Bricky. "They started selling in **1949**. Watch."

A worker stacked two bricks together, one on top of the other.

**Tap.** He let go.

**FLOP.** The top brick slid right off and rolled across the table.

Cruz burst out laughing. "That's just like my shark fin!"

"Exactly like your shark fin," said Bricky. "These bricks were a great start, but they wobbled loose. Somebody needed to figure out how to make them really, truly hold."

Phoenix stacked two blocks on the table and gave them a shake. **FLOP.** They fell too.

"Somebody should FIX that," Phoenix announced, hands on his hips.

"Somebody will," said Bricky, with a very knowing wiggle. "Let's go meet him."",
      "shout_line": "SOMEBODY SHOULD FIX THAT!"
    },
    {
      "heading": "Chapter 5: The Brick That Clicked",
      "text": "In the next workshop, a man named **Godtfred**, Ole Kirk's son, was frowning at two loose bricks in his hands.

"Toys should all connect to each other, every set to every other set," he muttered. "But these keep sliding apart. What's missing?"

Cruz picked up a brick and turned it upside down. He looked at the bumpy studs on top, then at the hollow, empty underneath.

"What if there was something **inside** here," Cruz said slowly, "to hug the bumps on the brick below?"

Godtfred froze. Then he grabbed a pencil and sketched little round **tubes** inside the bottom of the brick.

They built a brick with tubes inside. Phoenix held one brick in each hand and pressed them together.

**CLICK!**

He pulled. It held. He shook it hard. It still held! He turned it upside down and shook it even harder.

**IT STILL HELD!**

"IT CLICKS!" both boys shouted, jumping up and down on the workshop floor.

On **January 28, 1958**, that very brick was made official. And here's the wildest part: a brick from that day still clicks perfectly with a brick made today.",
      "shout_line": "IT CLICKS!"
    },
    {
      "heading": "Chapter 6: A Whole Land of Bricks",
      "text": "**BZZZT** — Bricky's glow turned bright and sparkly, and the workshop melted into something enormous: castles, dragons, whole towns, all built from tiny bricks stacked millions high.

"This is **LEGOLAND**," said Bricky. "It opened right here in Billund in **1968**, built from millions and millions of bricks."

A boy about Cruz's age ran past, holding a brand-new little yellow figure with a smiling face and bendy legs.

"That's **Kjeld**," said Bricky. "Godtfred's son. He tested new toys when he was a kid, just like you two are testing this whole adventure. He grew up and ran the entire company."

"Even the small guy gets a job?" asked Phoenix, pointing at the little yellow figure.

"Especially the small guy," said Bricky. "That's the LEGO **minifigure**. It showed up in **1978**, and people have been giving it every job in the world ever since — shark scientist, dinosaur digger, you name it."

Phoenix held his dinosaur toy next to the tiny minifigure and beamed like he'd found a new best friend.",
      "shout_line": "THE SMALL GUY GETS A JOB!"
    },
    {
      "heading": "Chapter 7: Back to the Floor",
      "text": "**WHOOOOSH!** The bright colors spun and swirled, and suddenly Cruz and Phoenix were sitting right back on the bedroom carpet, exactly where they started.

Bricky glowed softly beside them, looking very pleased with himself.

"Now you know the secret," Bricky said. "Try your shark again."

Cruz picked up his grey LEGO shark and pressed the fin down onto its little round studs. He thought about the tubes hiding inside, hugging the bumps tight, just like the ones he'd helped invent.

**CLICK!**

He shook it. He turned it upside down. He even gave it a gentle bounce on the carpet.

The fin stayed on.

"IT CLICKS!" Cruz whispered happily.

Phoenix set his dinosaur down next to the shark, guarding it like a very small, very fierce friend. Bricky's glow dimmed to a sleepy little flicker, tucking itself back among the other bricks on the floor.

"Goodnight, Bricky," Phoenix yawned.

And somewhere in the pile, one plain little brick winked one last time.",
      "shout_line": null
    }
  ],
  "ending_line": "Goodnight, Cruz. Goodnight, Phoenix. Play well.",
  "true_facts": [
    { "text": "LEGO began in **Billund, Denmark**, with a carpenter named **Ole Kirk Christiansen**, who started making wooden toys in **1932**.", "fact_id": "f1" },
    { "text": "One of Ole Kirk's first wooden toys was a **pull-along duck on wheels**.", "fact_id": "f3" },
    { "text": "Ole Kirk started making toys because during the hard 1930s, families didn't have money for new furniture.", "fact_id": "f4" },
    { "text": "The name **LEGO** comes from the Danish words ***leg godt***, meaning **"play well,"** chosen in **1934**.", "fact_id": "f2" },
    { "text": "Ole Kirk's motto was **"only the best is good enough,"** which he carved onto a sign.", "fact_id": "f6" },
    { "text": "The workshop burned down in **1942**, and nobody was hurt; Ole Kirk rebuilt it bigger.", "fact_id": "f5" },
    { "text": "The first plastic bricks, sold starting in **1949**, were called **Automatic Binding Bricks** and did not hold together well.", "fact_id": "f8" },
    { "text": "**Godtfred**, Ole Kirk's son, realized toys needed to all connect together as a system.", "fact_id": "f9" },
    { "text": "The fix was **hollow tubes** inside the underside of the brick, gripping the studs below.", "fact_id": "f10" },
    { "text": "The modern LEGO brick was patented on **January 28, 1958**, and old bricks still fit new ones.", "fact_id": "f11" },
    { "text": "**Kjeld Kirk Kristiansen**, Godtfred's son, tested toys as a boy and later ran the whole company.", "fact_id": "f12" },
    { "text": "**LEGOLAND** opened in Billund in **1968**, built from millions of bricks.", "fact_id": "f13" },
    { "text": "The LEGO **minifigure**, with its smiling face and bendy legs, arrived in **1978**.", "fact_id": "f14" }
  ],

    "ending_summary": "Cruz's LEGO shark finally clicked together and held, with Bricky the glowing brick settling back into the pile as Cruz and Phoenix drifted off to sleep."
